entry.title: The Delegation Divide: An Open Index of AI-Agent Delegability across Occupations and Countries
entry.summary:
35.2% of task time in world employment is at least partly delegable to AI agents in 2026, and only 2.5% can be handed over in full. Existing measures score exposure to generative AI, mostly for the United States. We build the Agent Delegability Index (ADI): two language models rate all 18,796 O*NET 30.2 task statements on a frozen, preregistered rubric of delegation levels and barriers; tasks are mapped to 433 ISCO-08 unit groups and weighted by ILOSTAT employment in 146 countries.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #ml-theory #consensus

entry.title: BitVM3: Efficient Bitcoin Bridges via Garbled Circuits
entry.summary:
Bitcoin bridges, protocols that lock BTC on Bitcoin and represent it on a secondary system, underpin much of Bitcoin's application layer, yet remain poorly secured. Deployed bridges rely on federated custody with honest-majority assumptions, while BitVM2, the state of the art in trust-minimized bridging, incurs worst-case dispute costs of approximately $16,000, requiring large operator bonds and deposits that restrict participation to well-capitalized parties. We present BitVM3-BRIDGE, a trust-minimized bridge architecture from Bitcoin to (i) chains with finality certificates, such as Ethereum, and (ii) Bitcoin rollups.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #consensus

entry.title: Network topology shapes consensus and vulnerability in LLM populations
entry.summary:
As large language models (LLMs) are deployed in interacting populations, their collective behaviour depends not only on the models but also on who interacts with whom. Studies of convention formation in LLM populations have mainly tested well-mixed interactions. We place policies extracted from four LLMs on fully connected, random regular, and heterogeneous networks, with $10^3$ to $10^5$ agents playing the naming game.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #consensus
